headline: South Asia: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
- Asia: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
- Africa: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Pentagon, Raytheon sign $6.3B deal to replenish US missile interceptor supply.
The contract "supports urgent replenishment of missile defense inventory that has been successfully used in combat," Raytheon said.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: Soldiers intervene on roadside to save children from alleged knife attack.
Three soldiers sprang into action when a highway crash in Washington turned into a knife attack on two children.
The Caribbean - bottom line: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: KIDD LANE  TERROR - Mom grieves for daughter who begged for help as triple murder rocks St Andrew community, forces residents to flee.
The frantic voice of her daughter pleading for help over the telephone moments before she was killed will forever haunt Natasha Hall. Hall’s daughter, 30-year-old Lashane Ellis, and her one-year-old grandson, Kaheel Daley, were killed on Friday night when armed men went to their home on Kidd Lane, off Spanish Town Road in St Andrew, opened fire and set the house ablaze. Before fleeing, the gunmen reportedly opened fire on a neighbouring house, killing 39-year-old Kimeisha Gibson.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Search and rescue operations following a Russian guided bomb attack on a Zaporizhzhia residential building ended – 23 people have been killed, including four children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Bomb disposal experts recover missile warhead from courtyard in Kyiv – photos, video.
Bomb disposal experts have recovered the warhead and non-explosive debris from a ballistic missile at the site of a Russian strike in the Obolonskyi district of Kyiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians strike two apartment blocks in Sloviansk: seven injured – photos, video.
Russian airstrikes hit two apartment blocks in Sloviansk, Donetsk Oblast, injuring seven people; Zelenskyy says residents may be trapped under rubble.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian drone hits car in Sumy Oblast, killing driver.
Regional authorities have reported that a Russian drone attack killed a driver in a civilian car in the Krasnopillia hromada, Sumy Oblast, near the Russian border.
Southern Europe - bottom line: ‘Putin will drag you into the war,’ former Ukrainian foreign minister tells Europeans.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: ‘Putin will drag you into the war,’ former Ukrainian foreign minister tells Europeans.
Dmytro Kuleba also said Ukraine will endure its worst winter yet as Russia targets the country's infrastructure in bid to break its resistance.
- Politico Europe, 12 hours ago: Russians face EU travel curbs to prevent hybrid attacks.
Tighter visa rules are expected to be proposed in January to bolster EU defenses against Russian threats.
- Politico Europe, 23 hours ago: Germany warns EU that €159B budget cuts are not enough.
Frugal countries said an end-of-year agreement is less likely after Ireland's proposal.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Sudan: Drone Strikes and Deadly Explosions Kill Scores of Civilians Across Sudan.
[Dabanga] Wad El Mahi Locality / Geisan Locality / El Roseir -- Drone strikes and explosions have killed scores of civilians and injured dozens across Sudan, as attacks on displacement shelters and residential neighbourhoods in Blue Nile and North Kordofan coincide with deadly mine blasts in West Kordofan and renewed armed violence in South Darfur.
- Africanews, 3 hours ago: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine.
Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.
- Africanews, one hour ago: Eritrea uges United Nations to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia.
The neighbours have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Ethiopia: UN Chief 'Gravely Concerned' By Renewed Fighting in Northern Ethiopia, Warns Against Escalation.
[UN News] UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an immediate end to the renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, saying he is deeply worried by reports that Eritrean forces are present in the country.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Russia’s Yandex says data centre in Vladimir shut down after drone attack.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Moscow Times, 5 hours ago: Russia’s Yandex says data centre in Vladimir shut down after drone attack.
Third strike on Yandex facilities in a week comes as Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks on tech infrastructure.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Fear and uncertainty for civilians as Yemen’s capital comes under attack.
Sanaa has faced intense bombing since the Yemeni government announced a campaign to take the capital from the Houthis.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: US Army urges adoption of Israeli battlefield medicine as IDF cuts casualty deaths by half - report.
According to data presented to Fox News, the mortality rate among combat casualties stood at approximately 15% during the Second Lebanon War in 2006.
- Jerusalem Post, 16 hours ago: Eisenkot demands decision on Netanyahu aide's alleged record alteration.
Eisenkot's appeal followed disclosures that Braverman acknowledged changing an official record of a conversation between Netanyahu and his military secretary on the morning of the October 7 attack.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize Is a Vote of Confidence in a Global Legal Order Under Fire.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: South Africa: Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize Is a Vote of Confidence in a Global Legal Order Under Fire.
[The Conversation Africa] The awarding of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to distinguished South African jurist and international judge Navanethem "Navi" Pillay is about more than just the recognition of an exceptional individual in the global fight for justice.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, NDTV - Top Stories, South China Morning Post - China, Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: Houthi strike on Riyadh airport kills 12; Saudi-led coalition vows 'decisive' response to worst attack on kingdom in a decade.
At least 12 people were killed and more than 300 wounded in an attack on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday, the deadliest in the kingdom in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalate a campaign they launched this summer. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. At the latest count, 309 were wounded, officials said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: FO reiterates Pakistan's 'firm and unshakeable' commitment to Saudi Arabia's security after Riyadh attack.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Sunday condemned a fresh wave of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, reaffirming Pakistan’s “firm and unshakeable” commitment to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and stability of the Gulf state under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The defence pact, of which Turkiye is also a part, was signed on August 7 and aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Asia - bottom line: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
- South China Morning Post - China, 6 hours ago: Can Saudi Arabia’s 2034 Fifa World Cup survive the Middle East’s escalating wars?.
When 60,000 football fans gathered in Jeddah for the Arabian Gulf Cup on Tuesday, they inadvertently highlighted the vulnerability of major sports events hosted by Gulf monarchies to the wars raging across the region. The previous day, Saudi Arabia resumed strikes on Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthi rebels after a four-year ceasefire collapsed. That truce had originally followed a Houthi attack on an oil facility near Jeddah’s Formula One track during a practice session. While the two-week football...
- South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: How Taiwan’s military manpower shortage is undermining its ability to fight.
Taiwan’s military is grappling with a worsening manpower shortage, with its volunteer staffing rate remaining below the 80 per cent target for a third consecutive year and concerns mounting over the impact on combat readiness, according to the island’s legislature. The shortages extend deep into frontline formations – including infantry, artillery, missile and air defence units – raising questions over whether Taiwan will have enough trained personnel to operate and maintain the vast quantities...
- South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: Spirit of Hong Kong Awards: Gaza nurse’s obstacle-laden road to becoming a professor.
On six occasions, Hammoda Abu-Odah, a Gaza nurse-turned Hong Kong scholar was offered an opportunity to study overseas. But each time, border closures and travel restrictions prevented him from taking them up. Abu-Odah had obtained a nursing degree in his native Gaza but set his sights on an academic career abroad. He kept working, teaching and conducting research, despite the many challenges that prevented him from leaving. Finally, on the seventh attempt, he made it to Hong Kong, where he...
- South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: Who rules Negeri Sembilan? Royal row tests Malaysia’s constitutional order.
The dust has yet to settle in Malaysia’s Negeri Sembilan, where a royal row has led to the fall of a state government and left the public wondering who, exactly, is in charge. Observers warn that the months-long constitutional crisis could create ripple effects well beyond the state’s borders, testing the entire nation’s systems of monarchy and government. The dispute centres on which of two men: the incumbent, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, or his intended replacement, Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku...
India - bottom line: AI, Nuclear War, Bioweapons May Trigger End Of Humanity By 2100: Report.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: AI, Nuclear War, Bioweapons May Trigger End Of Humanity By 2100: Report.
Nuclear war and the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) could put the future of humanity at risk, a new report stated.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Couple rejects $131,000 offer for data center power line on their property.
Jerry Zelenka has turned down American Transmission Company's proposal to place a power line on his property, citing worries over tree removal and the demolition of numerous buildings. He is particularly troubled by the level of compensation offered and the potential threat of eminent domain. Meanwhile, legal disputes from neighboring landowners about the project's validity persist.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Oregon blimp hangar sold for $1 after storm damage; air museum set to reopen.
An 83-year-old World War II-era blimp hangar in Oregon, US, was sold for just $1 after a storm tore a 200-foot hole in its roof in December 2025. The historic building, which houses the Tillamook Air Museum, was purchased by a nonprofit organisation and is set to reopen on October 29 after nearly 10 months of closure.
